properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): the orientation read was keyed to the user asking "where things stand" and to a session starting, never to the agent being about to ASSERT status; and the catalogue, asked in the asker's words for a progress deck, returned six tools of which none reads — routing was written from the design's side, not the asker's, and the read path has no demand
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL, the second walk of epoch:planned-the-mechanism-reaches-the-moment, on fact:field-report-hxm-a-progress-deck-was-written-from-a-checklist-and-recency-and-the-design-was-read-only-after-a-challenge (relayed by Anthony from the hxm_program hub design, 2026-09-14).

① OBSERVED: asked for a progress deck for management, the agent asserted the project's status from a script-by-script checklist file (boxes unticked by convention) and from the six change events it had itself written that week; it never read the design. Challenged, one topic call on the project's name gave 20 hits across 9 node types; it had known 6 of 41 change events. Expected: a status claim about a design under reflow2 is read from the design before it is written. NOT affected: the same agent opened the root-cause skill three times that month when a tool demanded it, so demands do reach it.

② PRECEDENT, searched: this is the FOURTH recorded instance of a class already on the record. fact:three-searches-that-did-not-happen-and-what-each-one-cost (2026-08-17): three assertions in prose about what the graph holds, none involving a tool call, "the write guard cannot fire because nothing was being written". dec:idea-search-first-fires-without-being-remembered: "ALL SIX HAPPENED ON THE READ PATH, WHERE NOTHING ENFORCES ANYTHING… it cannot fire when a user asks a question and an agent answers in prose", option A refused because "it needs to know what the user asked, which the tool layer never sees". fact:a-second-project-answered-what-is-left-to-build-from-decision-prose (2026-08-14): a status question answered from prose because the graph had no view for it. And fact:the-root-cause-skill-is-demanded-by-no-tool-and-named-by-no-trigger-so-it-loads-only-by-luck: a trigger keyed to the agent's internal state loads at 19-24 percent.

③ CANDIDATES from the bones: (a) ALLOCATION — the orientation skill's trigger is written for the user asking where things stand and for a session starting; the moment of asserting status is named nowhere. (b) ASSURANCE — nothing demands a read at the moment of a claim: only impact-check (record_change) and root-cause (record_finding) declare demanded_by; the nudge names where-am-i at SessionStart only. (c) CONTRACT — the catalogue (find_tools) is written from the design's side; the asker's words reach no reading tool. (d) INTENT/ABSENCE — nothing says how much of a subject the session has read (the recency mechanism that filled the vacuum). (e) NOT IN THE SUSPECTED COMPONENT — the project's own house rules pointed at the checklist file, a plan that reads as a status source. (f) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG.

④/⑤ MEASURED, 2026-09-14 on the checkout. (a) CONFIRMED: where-am-i's description read "Use when the user asks where things stand, what you've concluded, what's been decided, or wants to pick up an existing design after a break — and at the start of any session"; a request to produce a deck matches none of it. (b) CONFIRMED: grep of demanded_by across served skills — two skills, neither is orientation; tools/loop_nudge.py names where-am-i in SESSION_START_TEXT only; served AGENTS.md carries no "read before you assert status" rule. (c) CONFIRMED, the conversion test in the user's words: find_tools "put together a progress deck for management on what this project has achieved so far" → add_project, set_project_mode, schedule_for, set_violation_status, dimension_drifts, contains; "where does this project stand, what is done and what is still open" → add_project, set_project_mode, design_regions, open_questions, coverage_report, describe_schema. topic_report, the tool that answered after the challenge, in neither; its own catalogue query is "everything the design says about one subject in one place", nobody's phrasing of a status question. (d) CONFIRMED as absent (the usage ledger holds the verb, never the object) and recorded as an idea, not a cause: it is the mechanism that fills the vacuum once the read has not happened. (e) NOT MEASURABLE from here. (f) REFUTED: the session measured its own coverage, 6 of 41.

⑥ THE CLASS, sharpened from the precedent: the read path has no demand, and its two routing surfaces — the skill trigger and the tool catalogue — are written from the design's side ("where things stand", "one subject") rather than the asker's ("what have we achieved", "a deck for management"). The precedent said the tool layer never sees what the user asked; this instance shows the request WAS visible and matched nothing, which is a cheaper failure to fix than the internal-state one. Would this fix have stopped the 2026-08-17 three? Two of the three were the agent asserting what the graph holds with no user request to route, so no — those remain the internal-state class the root-cause precedent names. It would have stopped this one and the 2026-08-14 one, both of which began with a status question in a person's words.

⑦ PINNED FIRST: tools/skill_lint.py gained TRIGGER_CONTRACT (three phrases the orientation skill's DESCRIPTION must state — the part list_skills and the handshake serve) — observed failing, 3 checks. crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_status_question_in_the_askers_words_finds_the_read.rs (two queries in the asker's words must find topic_report in the top five) — observed failing, 0 passed 2 failed, with the same six tools measured by hand.

⑧ FIXED AT THE CAUSE, three legs. Instruction: the orientation skill's trigger (three mirrored copies) now says "and whenever you are about to assert the project's status to anyone: a progress report, a deck for management, a summary, 'what have we achieved'. The claim is the trigger, whoever asked and whoever the audience is; a status written from a checklist file or from what you wrote this week is a plan reported as a measurement" — served on every handshake through list_skills. Served tool: topic_report's description carries the asker's words and names itself the first read before a status is asserted; kept at its prior length (906 chars) because the first attempt at 1,350 chars knocked the tool out of the top five for its OWN query — the scorer penalises length, so the catalogue leg had to be a rewrite, not an addition. Detector: the lint contract, so the clause cannot lapse. All catalogue tests green (182 tools), lint green, snapshot and surface doc regenerated.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the hxm session would have loaded the skill given the new trigger (the served-prose load rate is measured at 19-24 percent where nothing demands it, and nothing demands orientation at the moment of a claim — no tool call marks it, the same limit the precedent names); whether a read-coverage line would change behaviour (dec:idea-reading-coverage-says-how-much-of-a-subject-this-session-has-actually-read stays an idea); the project-scoped rollup (dec:idea-a-project-scoped-status-rollup-answers-what-has-this-project-achieved-in-one-call) is the same ask as dec:idea-remaining-work-has-no-answer-in-the-graph's option (b) and stays for Anthony's word.
